**What Happened**

At 2026-10-02T15:13:44, a HighErrorRate alert was triggered for the `shop` service. Frontend nginx logs show continuous 502 responses for `/api/items` and other `/api/*` requests, with errors recurring on every load-generator request from 15:13:01 onward, including a live example at 15:14:11 referencing connection refused errors to upstream `10.96.35.67:8080` [7]. At the time of the alert, all pods in the `shop` namespace — including both `api` pods and both `frontend` pods — were reporting `Running` with zero restarts [5, 14].

**Root Cause**

The root cause was a selector mismatch on the `api` Service in the `shop` namespace. The Service's live selector was `app=api-v2` [10, 12], but both running `api` pods carry the label `app=api`, and no pod anywhere in the cluster carries the label `app=api-v2` [13, 14, 17]. As a result, the Service had zero endpoints [11], causing kube-proxy to refuse all connections to the ClusterIP and producing the 502 errors seen in the frontend nginx logs [7]. The Service's `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation confirms it was originally applied with selector `app: api`, matching the Deployment's pod template label [15, 16], indicating the live selector was changed via an untracked edit after initial deployment rather than being the intended configuration.

**Impact & Timeline**

All `/api/*` traffic proxied through the frontend was affected from at least 15:13:01 through the time of alert triggering and evidence collection, with 502 errors returned on every request [7]. The `frontend` and `redis` Services retained healthy endpoints throughout [11], confirming the outage was isolated to the `api` Service's routing path rather than a broader namespace failure.

## Ruled Out
- Pod crash or OOM — all `api` and `frontend` pods show `RESTARTS: 0` and `STATUS: Running` [5, 14]
- nginx configuration error on frontend — ConfigMap present and nginx startup/access logs show clean operation aside from the 502 upstream errors tied to the missing endpoints [7, 9]
- api application bug — `/healthz` endpoint returns 200 consistently inside the pod, and app logs are clean apart from a transient initial redis-connect retry that succeeded [8]
- Redis connectivity issue — initial connection failure was transient and resolved on retry, with no recurring errors [8]

## Not Checked
- Deployment rollout history for the `api` Deployment was not retrievable (`kubectl rollout history` blocked by mutating-kubectl policy) [18], so the exact timing/actor of the selector edit could not be confirmed

tool_input.content:
## Incident
KubePodNotReady alert: shop/worker new ReplicaSet pod (revision 2, e.g. worker-7fdf4ffb67-xxxx) stuck `Pending`, `Node: <none>`, `PodScheduled: False` for >5 min. Old revision-1 worker pod stayed Running/Ready throughout (not a full outage, just failed rollout of new replica).

## Root Cause
Live `worker` Deployment spec had `spec.template.spec.containers[0].resources.requests.cpu` set to `"64"` (64 **whole CPU cores**) instead of `"50m"` (50 millicores). The `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation on the same Deployment still showed `"50m"`, and the still-healthy revision-1 pod's actual resource request was confirmed as `50m` — proving this was an untracked live edit/drift, not a reviewed `kubectl apply` or Deployment YAML change.

Cluster nodes (`aurora-lab-worker`, `aurora-lab-worker2`) each have only 10 allocatable CPUs; `aurora-lab-control-plane` is tainted NoSchedule (normal/expected, unrelated). A request of 64 cores can never be satisfied by any node, so the scheduler permanently rejects the pod: `FailedScheduling: 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient cpu.`

## How to Diagnose Fast
1. `kubectl get pods -n shop -o wide` — identify the Pending pod, confirm `Node: <none>`.
2. `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n shop` — check `Events: FailedScheduling` reason text (Insufficient cpu/memory vs taint vs affinity).
3. Compare `resources.requests` in `kubectl get deployment <name> -n shop -o yaml` spec vs the `last-applied-configuration` annotation — a mismatch confirms live-edit drift (recurring org pattern in shop namespace).
4. Confirm node allocatable capacity with `kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.allocatable.cpu}'` to quantify how far off the request is.

## Fix (requires write access — blocked under read-only policy)
`kubectl patch deployment worker -n shop --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/cpu","value":"50m"}]'`
Low risk — reverts to the known-good, previously-applied value also present on the still-running revision-1 pod.

## Pattern Note
This is the 9th distinct root-cause mechanism identified in the shop namespace's recurring "untracked live-edit drift" incident family (see also: liveness probe port 8081 vs 8080, Service selector app=api-v2, missing DB_PASSWORD Secret, frontend image tag typo, nginx ConfigMap proxy_conect_timeout typo, log-shipper sidecar OOM, worker BATCH_SIZE OOM). Common thread: `last-applied-configuration` annotation retains the correct/reviewed value while the live object has been hand-edited to an incorrect one — always diff these two before trusting the live spec.

Investigation Summary

Hypothesis tested: worker pod Pending >5min → likely scheduling failure (resource request, taint, or capacity issue), given this namespace's history of untracked live-edit drift (api liveness port, api Service selector, api DB_PASSWORD secret, frontend image tag/ConfigMap typo). Checked history first — no prior incident matches worker-Pending-via-scheduling, so this is a new mechanism.

Evidence gathered:
kubectl get pods -n shop -o wide → worker-7fdf4ffb67-cvrt2 is 0/1 Pending, NODE: <none>, age 62s (matches alert's ">5 min Pending" trajectory). All other shop pods (api, frontend, redis, loadgen, and the other worker pod worker-6cf88d4b58-rfbzp) are Running.
kubectl describe pod worker-7fdf4ffb67-cvrt2 -n shop → Conditions: PodScheduled False, Event: FailedScheduling: 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient cpu. preemption: 0/3 nodes are available: 3 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling. Pod spec shows Requests: cpu: 64, memory: 64Mi.
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath=...allocatable.cpu → aurora-lab-worker and aurora-lab-worker2 each have only 10 allocatable CPUs; aurora-lab-control-plane carries the NoSchedule taint (the "1 untolerated taint" node — expected/benign).
kubectl get deployment worker -n shop -o yaml → live spec: resources.requests.cpu: "64". The kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration annotation on the same object shows the originally applied value was requests.cpu: "50m".
Cross-check: the still-Running revision-1 pod worker-6cf88d4b58-rfbzp has resources.requests.cpu: "50m" (confirmed via kubectl get pod ... -o jsonpath), matching the last-applied-configuration — proving 50m was the intended/working value and 64 (interpreted as 64 whole cores, not 64m) is a live drift, not a reviewed change.

Root cause (CONFIRMED): The live worker Deployment object was edited outside of kubectl apply to set the worker container's resources.requests.cpu from 50m to 64 (64 full CPU cores instead of 64

Final Conclusion — CONFIRMED

Root cause: The live shop/worker Deployment's container resources.requests.cpu was drifted (via untracked live edit, not a tracked kubectl apply) from the correct 50m to "64" — i.e., 64 whole CPU cores instead of 64 millicores, a ~1,280x increase. Both schedulable nodes (aurora-lab-worker, aurora-lab-worker2) have only 10 allocatable CPUs each, so the scheduler can never place the pod. This produces the exact alert condition: worker-7fdf4ffb67-cvrt2 stuck Pending with Node: <none> and event FailedScheduling: 0/3 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint(s), 2 Insufficient cpu.

Evidence trail:
Pod worker-7fdf4ffb67-cvrt2: Status: Pending, PodScheduled: False, requests cpu: 64.
Deployment live spec: requests.cpu: "64" vs. last-applied-configuration annotation (same object): cpu: "50m".
Still-healthy revision-1 pod worker-6cf88d4b58-rfbzp: actual request confirmed as 50m via kubectl get pod -o jsonpath — proves 50m is the known-good value.
Node allocatable CPU confirmed at 10 cores per node via kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath.

Ruled out: node readiness (all 3 Ready), image pull issues, ConfigMap/secret errors (pod never reached container-start stage), control-plane taint as root cause (expected/benign, unrelated to the two schedulable nodes' failure).

Impact: No outage — the old revision-1 worker pod kept running and processing. This is a stuck rollout of the new replica, isolated to worker; api/frontend/redis/loadgen all healthy.

Fix (blocked by read-only policy — requires engineer with write access):
``
kubectl patch deployment worker -n shop --type=json \
  -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/requests/cpu","value":"50m"}]'
`
Validated: confirmed container index/path via live YAML, confirmed 50m` is correct via last-applied-configuration + the running revision-1 pod's actual request. Low risk, straightforward revert.
